quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows down your motorcycle like braking does. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What lane position is best?

options.text: One that reduces your space cushion and lets others see you.
One that increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
One that puts you in more danger and lets others pass you.
One that reduces danger but requires you to follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: The best lane position gives you more space around you and makes you visible to other drivers. It helps you avoid other drivers' blind spots, road hazards, and wind blasts. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: How should a rider sit on a motorcycle for best control?

options.text: Using arms to hold the body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep your arms slightly bent on the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Increase speed to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the gas and ride straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: What is another name for downshifting to a lower gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear works like braking. That is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: Why should inexperienced riders ride near the front of a group?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They will slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them easily.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are white with black letters or symbols. They show road rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane
In the left portion of the lane
As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you
Without signaling, so you do not distract the other driver

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass only when it is safe. Then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, even if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Focus on moving through the intersection quickly.
Speed up so others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists and still miss them. Always slow down when you approach an intersection.

questions.question: When you are turning, what happens to your stopping ability?

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping.
There is more grip available for stopping.
Stopping works the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful. When a motorcycle leans to turn, some grip is used for the turn. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: What should a passenger do?

options.text: Lean with the operator when turning.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator when turning.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit as far forward as they can without bothering the operator. They should hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: As you slow down or stop, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your bike will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start slowing sooner, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the bike and should always lean with the operator. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: To find how much alcohol remains, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: Which one is not protective clothing for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, full-fingered gloves, and heavy denim pants protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or sturdy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the next lane as possible. A mirror may show the edge of your arm, but the most important thing is seeing the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have ridden for less than six months. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting the object. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat and roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before impact.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Most crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle. Take extra care when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and downward. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not accelerate or use the brakes, as these will make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups should switch to single-file formation when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. A staggered formation is used at other times.
